correctness.rationale: Each sampled cyclic gap has the joint Dirichlet(1,...,1) law. The inscribed-angle formula makes a vertex acute exactly when its two adjacent gap sum exceeds 1/2. Any two nonadjacent such events are impossible; hence the two-acute event has a unique neighboring pair. A unit-Jacobian transformation of the three relevant gaps leads to an explicit s-integral; evaluating it proves the density and pair mass 2^(2-n). The two triangular sections give a product density under maximum and ratio. Beta moments, covariance and beta-to-gamma limit follow by exact integration. The standalone Python standard-library checker passed 1,251 exact and sampled assertions for supporting finite cases; the analytic proof covers all n and the limit. Endpoints and right-angle ties have zero probability.

originality.rationale: The December 3, 2005 Putnam A6 solutions prove only the acute-count event and adjacent-pair geometry, without the conditional two-deficit law. Finch (arXiv:1610.00510, Sections 2 and 4) derives joint angle laws for n=4 and n=5, which are acknowledged as previously analyzed special sizes, but provides no formula for all n, the beta–uniform factorization or the joint rare-event asymptotic. Actual research-record queries about angle defects and adjacent exceedances did not return an all-n statement. The all-n family is not logically implied merely by the scalar count or finite-order angle densities; its three-gap integration is a separate calculation. Historical priority remains qualified by possible unknown general Dirichlet identities.
residual_risks: An older all-n theorem may be phrased as a joint Dirichlet linear-combination distribution and contain the same result without using polygon-angle terminology.
Accessible Finch text lists earlier Dirichlet linear-combination references (1976, 2000) not fully inspected; these supply general tools and might contain directly usable transforms.
The novel contribution is the general rare-event conditional geometry and exact beta–uniform factorization; fixed n=4 (and possibly n=5) consequences are already implied by known angle distributions.
Same-model originality review only; absolute historical novelty is not independently certified.

value.rationale: Rare two-acute configurations of cyclic polygons occur with exponentially small probability, so their conditional geometry is not explained by the classical event-count probability. An exact joint density gives the dependence and scale of the two rare extreme vertex-angle defects; the independent uniform deficit ratio, beta maximum, nontrivial positive limiting correlation 3/7 and universal gamma-shaped joint limit provide natural structural descriptors for rare polygon shapes. This is an all-n classification of a geometrically canonical marked configuration, not a recomputation of the known scalar event or an arbitrary finite slice.
